key_insight: For linear-elastic homogenization, differentiating a two-local Ising Hamiltonian yields one-local stress observables readable from the same computational-basis measurements as the energy.
engineering_relevance: The formulation enables direct extraction of effective stress from an optimized quantum state without reconstructing microscopic displacements or adding a measurement basis.
method: Encode the reduced finite-element RVE energy as a QUBO and map it to an Ising Hamiltonian.
Approximate the equilibrium ground state using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE).
Apply Hellmann–Feynman differentiation with respect to macroscopic strain to obtain stress observables.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a two-dimensional periodic RVE but provides no quantitative accuracy, scaling, or hardware results.
watch_item: Stress accuracy requires validation against encoding discretization and approximate VQE convergence; the abstract establishes no quantum speedup.
paper_title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable
